sources.title: Issues and strategies for the physical design of system-on-a-chip ASICs
sources.venue_or_publication: IBM Journal of Research and Development, vol. 46, no. 6, pp. 661-674
sources.what_it_covers: SoC ASIC physical-design infrastructure: functional libraries, physical conventions, hierarchical design, placement, routing, verification, electrical robustness, and packaging.
sources.why_relevant: Directly nameable ASIC physical-design closure source; useful for congestion/timing/power-grid methodology rather than a single anecdote.
sources.verification_hint: "Issues and strategies for the physical design of system-on-a-chip ASICs" "10.1147/rd.466.0661"

sources.title: Overview of the architecture, circuit design, and physical implementation of a first-generation cell processor
sources.venue_or_publication: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits, vol. 41, no. 1, pp. 179-196
sources.what_it_covers: First-generation Cell processor architecture, circuit design, and physical implementation across PPE/SPE cores, memory hierarchy, power/clocking, and implementation tradeoffs.
sources.why_relevant: Detailed design-closure account of a difficult high-frequency multicore ASIC; good comparator for timing, power-grid, and integration pressure.
sources.verification_hint: "Overview of the architecture, circuit design, and physical implementation of a first-generation cell processor" "179-196"

sources.title: Design and migration challenges for an Alpha microprocessor in a 0.18μm copper process
sources.venue_or_publication: IEEE International Solid-State Circuits Conference, Digest of Technical Papers, pp. 320-321, 460
sources.what_it_covers: Migration of a high-performance Alpha microprocessor to a 0.18 μm copper process, emphasizing redesign/reclosure challenges rather than architecture.
sources.why_relevant: Process-migration war-story adjacent to, but distinct from, the owned Alpha 21264 IEEE Micro paper; relevant to timing, interconnect, noise, and physical redesign.
sources.verification_hint: "Design and migration challenges for an Alpha microprocessor in a 0.18" ISSCC 2001 320 321 460

sources.title: The Pentium Chronicles: The People, Passion, and Politics Behind Intel's Landmark Chips
sources.what_it_covers: First-person history of Intel P6/Pentium Pro-era development: architecture decisions, validation, schedule pressure, team dynamics, and Pentium-bug aftermath.
sources.why_relevant: A nameable design-war-story source for closure under schedule/validation pressure; treat FDIV root-cause claims as contested and cross-check against Coe/Shirriff.
sources.verification_hint: "The Pentium Chronicles" "People, Passion, and Politics" Colwell Wiley IEEE 2006

sources.title: Intel's $475 million error: the silicon behind the Pentium division bug
sources.what_it_covers: Die-level analysis of the Pentium FDIV PLA: where the bug sits on silicon, extracted transistor patterns, missing lookup-table cells, Intel's fix, IBM's counter-analysis, and recall impact.
sources.why_relevant: Public postmortem connecting silicon bring-up failure to root cause and recovery; also corrects/contests official and memoir explanations.
sources.verification_hint: "Intel's $475 million error" "silicon behind the Pentium division bug" righto.com

sources.title: Statistical Analysis of Floating Point Flaw in the Pentium Processor
sources.venue_or_publication: Intel Corporation white paper / technical report, H. P. Sharangpani and M. L. Barton, Nov. 30, 1994
sources.what_it_covers: Intel's official statistical impact analysis of the Pentium FDIV flaw, explanation of the PLA/table omission, risk claims, and replacement-policy rationale.
sources.why_relevant: Primary public postmortem for the canonical silicon failure/recovery episode; best read alongside Shirriff/Coe because its root-cause framing is disputed.
sources.verification_hint: "Statistical Analysis of Floating Point Flaw in the Pentium Processor" Sharangpani Barton Intel November 30 1994
